problem: CKA-DONOR: donor-aware, bias-corrected and exactly calibrated representation similarity (CKA) between frozen encoders when spots are nested in few donors
source: Groger, Wen, Brbic (arXiv:2602.14486), "Limitations and outlook": the calibrated/debiased similarity guarantees assume exchangeability, so grouped or clustered samples require restricted permutations that preserve the dependence structure (stated, not done). Corroboration: PathoROB (arXiv:2507.17845) finds centre information pervasive in 20 pathology-FM embeddings; CRoMa (arXiv:2607.25497) lists needing known confounder labels as a limitation.
formulation: Spots i nested in donors g(i), G=5-25 donors; encoder features X_i, Y_i. Target = donor-population similarity, not spot-population. Centred cross-covariance splits exactly as C = C_B + C_W (between-donor means, within-donor deviations; X_B^T Y_W = 0), so linear HSIC = ||C_B||^2 + ||C_W||^2 + 2<C_B,C_W> (identity checked numerically on random data: between share 0.80, within 0.13, cross 0.07). Estimands: pooled CKA, within-donor CKA, between-donor CKA, and their ratio form; null = no alignment beyond donor structure.
closest_prior: Independence-test half is TAKEN: Liu et al. NeurIPS 2021 and the Sci Rep 2022 fast version give HSIC tests for cluster-correlated data (asymptotic null, large-cluster regime). Also: Schutt et al. eLife 2023 (2-factor bootstrap for RSA with subjects and stimuli random effects), Chwialkowski et al. arXiv:1408.5404 (wild bootstrap for dependent data), Murphy 2405.01012 and Chun 2502.15104 (debiased CKA for i.i.d. samples), Groger 2602.14486 itself. Not found: CKA (ratio) estimand under donor nesting with between/within split, few-donor exact calibration, or any histology-encoder application. The algebraic decomposition is trivial; novelty would rest on (ii)-(iii). 10 web + 5 arXiv/other queries.

problem: WINNER-FEW: inference on the winning encoder/configuration when candidate losses are near rank-one dependent and the covariance is estimated from G donors
source: Zrnic & Fithian (arXiv:2411.18569), Discussion: the hybrid method is the most powerful when a normal approximation with known covariance is available, struggles with many clearly suboptimal candidates, and the zoom correction reverts to a union bound under unknown dependence. Bakshi et al. (arXiv:2607.18545) list power gains without extra conditioning and follow-up questions as future directions; Xu et al. (arXiv:2605.05973) leave open-ended adaptive search to future work; Andrews-Kitagawa-McCloskey and the multiple-winners paper (arXiv:2410.19212) treat the covariance as known.
formulation: Candidates m=1..M (10 encoders, optionally x PCA dimension x ridge penalty); donors d=1..G are i.i.d. units with per-donor skill vector s_d in R^M; theta_m = E s_{d,m}; winner m_hat = argmax of the donor-mean. Targets: theta_{m_hat}, the identity set of population winners, and the gap to the runner-up. Sigma_hat has rank <= G-1 and entries near 1 (rank-one skill).
closest_prior: Occupied at generic level: Andrews et al. (conditional/hybrid), Zrnic-Fithian, Bakshi et al., SIREN (adaptive benchmarking), Wei et al. arXiv:2206.11868 (estimated covariance, growing dimension). Classical multiple-comparison-with-the-best procedures (reality-check, superior-predictive-ability, model-confidence-set families) are known to me but were NOT retrieved in this session and must be verified. No cluster-level treatment with G<M or rank-one dependence found in 2 targeted web queries. Adjacent to excluded BENCH: it differs because the target is selected-winner inference (selection bias), not the pairwise encoder difference.

problem: SPECSHARE: debiased inference on the rank and rank-one share of a model x gene/task skill matrix whose noise comes from shared test donors
source: Low-rank evaluation papers fix rank heuristically or assume it and treat noise as i.i.d.: Maimon et al. (arXiv:2507.20208) pick the number of factors by the Kaiser rule and an 85 percent cumulative-variance threshold; Li, Simchi-Levi, Sun (arXiv:2605.29395, arXiv:2604.05460) assume a known rank with i.i.d. BTL comparisons and I found no explicit limitations passage; Hardy et al. (arXiv:2605.25272, search excerpt only) say benchmark noise sources and magnitudes remain unquantified. The gap is therefore my paraphrase of an omission, not an authors quoted limitation.
formulation: S in R^{genes x encoders}: donor-population per-gene skill (e.g. within-donor correlation). Observed S_hat = mean over G donors of s_d, with noise E = S_hat - S dependent across genes and encoders through the shared donors. Estimands: rank r(S), top share rho_1 = sigma_1^2/||S||_F^2 (project data: PC1 share 0.93-0.98 across 3 encoders x 6 tasks), with and without removal of a donor-level nuisance factor.
closest_prior: Generic problem occupied: factor-number selection under strongly correlated errors (Bai-Ng 2002, Ahn-Horenstein 2013, Onatski, Lam-Yao, Lin-Michailidis arXiv:1912.04123), bootstrap PCA eigenvalue CIs (Fisher et al. arXiv:1405.0922), Horn parallel analysis (used in arXiv:2602.15532), rank tests under noise (arXiv:2601.08353). Not found: resampling unit = test donor shared by all models/items, debiased spectral share in an evaluation matrix. Likely reduces to a corollary of cluster bootstrap plus a delta-method unless a sharp finite-G or identifiability result emerges. 3 web + 4 arXiv queries.

problem: TWOLEVEL: two-level (donors x spots per donor) learning curves for frozen-encoder probes, with extrapolation intervals and an interchangeability boundary
source: Nezhurina et al. (arXiv:2506.04598), Discussion: accurate scaling laws need dense small-scale measurements and fitting routines that extrapolate accurately (future work); Kricheli et al. (arXiv:2605.08541), Limitations: their theorem gives an ordering not a magnitude and the corollary assumes i.i.d. Gaussian residuals. Ooi et al. (Nature 2025, excerpts only) derive a sample-size versus scan-time model for connectome prediction; I did not read their limitations.
formulation: Risk R(G,m) of a ridge probe trained on G donors with m spots each, tested on a new donor. Working model R = R_inf + a G^-alpha + b (G m)^-beta + donor-level term; targets alpha, the boundary m*(G) beyond which more spots per donor stop substituting for donors, the cost-optimal allocation, and the extrapolated risk at G* > G_obs. Learning-curve points use nested subsets of the same donors, hence are dependent.
closest_prior: Theory largely occupied: Atanasov et al. arXiv:2408.04607 (ridge risk and CV with correlated samples), Patil-Du-Tibshirani arXiv:2404.01233 (ridge for OOD), Dabo-Bigot arXiv:2403.20200 (ridge with variance profile, random effects), Ooi et al. (N versus per-subject data). Not found: extrapolation CIs for donor-level learning curves, or an application to frozen pathology encoders. Formal novelty is thin; risk of being a mixed-model design-effect corollary. 3 web + 4 arXiv queries.

problem: EMBED-DML: transferability test and cluster-level cross-fitting for frozen-embedding controls when embeddings encode donor identity
source: Shimizu (arXiv:2607.17378): uniform convergence rate over the estimated set of embedding functions, relaxing the strong density-ratio condition, and rates for regularised neural-network target estimators are left to future research; the multiplier-bootstrap transferability test is proven for a single nuisance-training block (the cross-fitted version needs a separate argument); the theory assumes an i.i.d. target sample, with requester clustering used only in the application.
formulation: Partially linear model Y_i = theta X_i + g(E(W_i)) + U_i with E a frozen encoder (10 choices), observations nested in G donors; embeddings predict donor identity (PathoROB), so cross-fitted g can use donor fingerprints; theta = within-donor effect of a spot-level covariate (nuclear morphology) on expression.
closest_prior: Largely taken: multiway-cluster DML (Chiang et al. arXiv:1909.03489), panel DML with fixed effects (Clarke-Polselli arXiv:2312.08174; Fuhr-Papies arXiv:2409.01266), interactive-fixed-effects DML with N=20 units and cluster-robust variance (arXiv:2608.01137), subject-level block cross-fitting in software (arXiv:2512.15965 excerpt). The only remainder is the embedding-specific transferability test under clustering, a plausible straightforward extension. 1 web query plus the Shimizu text.
